title: Relink a 230/400 V motor for a 400 V supply: star, not delta
instruction: Link this 230/400 V motor for its new 400 V supply.
context: A three-phase motor rated 230/400 V runs in delta on a 230 V supply and in star on 400 V. When a motor moves to a 400 V supply, its terminal links must be changed: left in delta, each winding gets root 3 times its rated voltage and burns out within minutes; a link left on the line row while the star is made shorts the supply. The electrician lifts the three delta links off, bridges the winding-end row with two of them and keeps the third in the box lid. Done by: industrial electricians, motor repair and commissioning technicians.
setup: On the table, centred 34 cm in front of the arm bases and 12 cm right of centre, is the open terminal box of a three-phase motor: a grey terminal board 16 x 16 x 3 cm (20 kg) inside 2 cm grey walls, with six brass studs 8 mm across and 1.5 cm tall in the IEC layout, 4.5 cm apart both ways: U1 V1 W1 in the far row (left to right as the robot sees it), where three black supply leads come in from a cable gland in the left wall, and W2 U2 V2 in the near row. Behind it lies the motor (blue finned frame 11 x 20 x 12 cm, black fan cowl on the right, steel shaft on the left, nameplate on top). Three brass links (6.5 x 2 x 0.4 cm, 40 g, two 12 mm square holes 4.5 cm apart, a black insulated handle 2 x 1.5 x 5 cm between them) stand on the studs in delta: U1-W2, V1-U2, W1-V2. The box's lid (12 x 12 cm, 1.2 cm rim) lies upside down 38 cm out and 28 cm right of centre.
scoring: A link is on a stud pair when both hole centres are within 4 mm of the two studs, its plate's bottom within 9 mm of the board (room for a second link stacked at U2) and it tilts at most 8 degrees; it is in the lid when its centre is inside the rim and within 2 cm of the lid's floor. At the end of the trial: 0 if any link is anywhere other than the star pairs W2-U2, U2-V2 or the lid; otherwise 1.0 if both star pairs are bridged, 0.6 if one is, 0.3 if none (all links in the lid). The trial ends 1 s after 1.0 is reached.
reset_notes: Stand the three links back on the studs in delta (U1-W2, V1-U2, W1-V2) and empty the lid.
fidelity: Off-circuit work, so only the final state is scored. Real links are held by nuts and need a spanner; here they drop over plain studs with 2 mm of clearance and an upright insulated handle stands in for the electrician's fingers. The stud letters are not printed (unreadable at 320 x 176); the layout is the IEC standard and the supply leads mark the line row.
